To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the synthesis of amphipathic carotenoid–dihydroflavonoid hybrids and carotenoid–triazole-dihydroflavone conjugates was achieved by the Cu-catalyzed azide–alkyne [4+2] cyclo-addition reaction and that these hybrids showed higher antioxidant activity and different aggregation profiles depending on the type of flavonoid, the position of the phenolic hydroxys, and the type of the applied polar aprotic

the synthesis of carotenoid–dihydroxyflavonoid hybrids was achieved by the Cu(I) catalyzed azide-alkynes [3 + 2] dipolar cycloaddition, and their antioxidant properties and self-assembly were examined in detail.
amphipathic carotenoid–triazole conjugates of flavonoids were obtained and their antioxidant properties and self-assembly behavior were studied.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the synthesis of novel amphipathic carotenoid–polyphenol hybrids and their antioxidant properties, as well the self-assembly of zeaxanthol conjugates in different solvents.
the synthesis of new carotenoid–triazole–flavonoids with different antioxidant properties and self-assembly behavior.
the synthesis and evaluation of new amphiphilic carotenoid–polyphenol conjugates, and the study of their self-assembly in different solvents.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the antioxidant properties of the conjugates are not only determined by the individual antioxidant properties of the parent compounds, but also by their self-assembly properties.
the antioxidant capacity of the carotenoid–triazole–flavonoids is higher than that of their corresponding parent compounds.
the antioxidant activity is strongly influenced by the type of the carotenoid and flavonoid, the type of the solvent, and the type of the conjugate.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the antioxidant capacity of the carotenoid–dihydroflavonoid hybrids is higher than that of the carotenoids, while the antioxidant capacity of their dihydroflavonoid analogues is lower than that of their parent flavonoid.

amphipathic flavonoid–zeaxanthin hybrids are promising candidates for self-assembly in polar solvents, and that the position of the hydroxyl group of flavonoids has a profound effect on the aggregation of the hybrids.
the amphipathic flavonoid–zeaxanthin conjugates are capable of forming J-aggregate structures in aprotic polar solvents.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the covalent attachment of a flavonoid to a carotenoid does not necessarily result in an enhancement of the antioxidant properties.

the covalent conjugation of carotenoids and flavonoids can lead to the formation of novel hybrid molecules with enhanced antioxidant activity and self-assembly properties, which can be further exploited for biomedical and nanotechnological applications.
the antioxidant capacity of carotenoids can be modulated by the formation of conjugates with flavonoids, which may be of interest in the design of new antioxidant compounds.
